This rule is part of the [nursery](/linter/#nursery) group. This means that it is experimental and the behavior can change at any time.
:::
## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.6.5`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/useVueBooleanPropTypeFirst`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule has an [**unsafe**](/linter/#unsafe-fixes) fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**warning**](/reference/diagnostics#warning).
- This rule belongs to the following domains:
  - [`vue`](/linter/domains#vue)
- Sources: 
  - Same as [`vue/prefer-prop-type-boolean-first`](https://eslint.vuejs.org/rules/prefer-prop-type-boolean-first)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"useVueBooleanPropTypeFirst": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Require `Boolean` to be the first type of Vue props that accept several types.

A prop can accept several types by listing them in an array, such as
`[Boolean, String]`. When a Boolean prop is written in a template without a value, as in
`<MyComponent disabled />`, Vue sets it to `true`. However, if `String` comes before
`Boolean` in the list, Vue sets the prop to an empty string instead. Writing `Boolean`
first makes such a prop behave the same as a prop that only accepts `Boolean`.

This rule checks props declared through the `props` option and `defineProps()`.

## Examples

### Invalid

```vue
<script>
export default {
  props: {
    disabled: [String, Boolean],
  },
};
</script>
```

### Valid

```vue
<script setup>
defineProps({
  disabled: Boolean,
  label: String,
  loading: [Boolean, String],
  size: { type: [Boolean, String, Number] },
});
</script>
```
